module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 7

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/7](https://www.erdosproblems.com/7)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos7

open Set

/--
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd (and greater than 1)?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_7 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (C : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ), ∀ i,
      ¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2} ∧ C.moduli i ≠ ⊤ := by
  sorry

end Erdos7

findings.description: The theorem docstring reads "Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd (and greater than 1)?" and leaves out the word "distinct". The source has that word, and the Lean statement enforces it through `StrictCoveringSystem.injective_moduli`. Under the common modern meaning of "covering system" (repeated moduli allowed), the docstring asks a trivial question. I checked in Lean that 0, 1, 2 (mod 3) is a `CoveringSystem ℤ` whose moduli are all odd and not ⊤. The Lean statement itself is correct, so the mathematics is unaffected. Only the prose is less precise than the source. It can be defended under Erdős's own convention, which the `StrictCoveringSystem` docstring cites and in which covering systems have distinct moduli.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/7 (live page): "Is there a distinct covering system all of whose moduli are odd?". Filaseta–Ford–Konyagin, Illinois J. Math. 2000 (https://ford126.web.illinois.edu/wwwpapers/ffk.pdf): "determine whether a covering of the integers exists for which the indices j range over a finite set and the m_j are distinct odd integers > 1".
findings.suggested_fix: Docstring: "Is there a distinct covering system (a finite system of congruences with pairwise distinct moduli, all greater than 1) all of whose moduli are odd?" No change to the Lean statement.

reformulations.difference: The source's conditions are written in terms of ideals, not integers. "All moduli odd" is `¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2}`. This is ideal inclusion (n) ⊆ (2), i.e. 2 ∣ n; it is NOT the numeric bound n ≤ 2, so a reader could mistake it for "modulus > 2". "Distinct moduli" is injectivity of `moduli : ι → Ideal ℤ`. "Moduli > 1" comes from the structure's `ne_top`, and the theorem repeats it with a redundant conjunct `C.moduli i ≠ ⊤`. Nonzero moduli come from `ne_bot`, and finiteness from `Fintype ι`. Each residue class is the coset `{a} + (n)`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument:
ℤ is a PID. Every ideal equals (n) for a unique n : ℕ, the natAbs of the generator, by `Int.span_natAbs` and `Ideal.span_singleton_generator`. Then:
- (n) ≠ ⊥ ⟺ n ≠ 0, and (n) ≠ ⊤ ⟺ n ≠ 1 (`Int.isUnit_iff`).
- (n) ≤ (2) ⟺ 2 ∣ n (`Ideal.span_singleton_le_span_singleton`).
- (m) = (n) ⟺ m = n for m, n : ℕ (`Int.associated_iff_natAbs`).
- {a} + (n) = a + nℤ.
I proved in Lean, using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound: `(∃ C : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, ∀ i, ¬ C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2} ∧ C.moduli i ≠ ⊤) ↔ ∃ S : Finset (ℤ × ℕ), (∀ p ∈ S, 1 < p.2 ∧ Odd p.2) ∧ Set.InjOn Prod.snd (S : Set (ℤ × ℕ)) ∧ ∀ x : ℤ, ∃ p ∈ S, x ≡ p.1 [ZMOD p.2]`. The right-hand side is exactly FFK00's "odd covering": finitely many congruences whose moduli are distinct odd integers > 1 and which cover ℤ. It is also the source's "distinct covering system all of whose moduli are odd".

review.notes:
The file has one declaration, `Erdos7.erdos_7`. The Lean statement matches the source, and the equivalence with the elementary formulation is proved in /workspace/review/equiv.lean.

Checks in /workspace/review/sanity.lean:
- `StrictCoveringSystem ℤ` can be built (the classic distinct covering 0 (2), 0 (3), 1 (4), 5 (6), 7 (12)), so the right-hand side does not hold or fail trivially because the structure is empty.
- A non-strict `CoveringSystem ℤ` with odd moduli exists (0, 1, 2 mod 3), so the distinctness that `StrictCoveringSystem` imposes is essential and is correctly included.

The conjunct `C.moduli i ≠ ⊤` repeats the structure's `ne_top` and does no harm.

Under the repository's default `answer` setting (`alwaysTrue`), `answer(sorry)` elaborates to `True`. This is repository machinery, not a defect in this file.

Polarity: the right-hand side is the existence statement, which is the source's affirmative, so the conjecture is not negated.

Status: the source says VERIFIABLE (open, provable by a finite example), and the file's `research open` matches it.
